Digital Image Forensics Tool

Analyze image metadata, generate SHA-256 integrity hashes, and compare files — all locally in your browser.

3. Error Level Analysis (ELA)

Error Level Analysis recompresses a JPEG image at a known quality level and compares the result to the original. Brighter areas in the visualization indicate regions that responded differently to recompression, which may suggest editing — though many factors can cause this.

Original Image

ELA Visualization

How to read this

Brighter (whiter) areas in the ELA visualization represent higher error levels — those regions reacted differently when the image was recompressed. Uniformly textured areas (like sky or flat surfaces) typically appear dark and consistent. Edited or pasted regions may appear brighter or show different patterns than surrounding areas.

Important: ELA highlights compression differences and cannot conclusively prove image manipulation. Many legitimate factors — compression history, image content, resaving — can produce similar patterns. This is an investigative aid, not definitive evidence.
